assertions.description: AbortController.abort(reason) stores an arbitrary reason on signal.reason.
assertions.test: (() => { const c = new AbortController(); const marker = { probe: 'conformance' }; c.abort(marker); return c.signal.aborted && c.signal.reason === marker; })()

assertions.description: abort() with no argument defaults signal.reason to an "AbortError" DOMException.
assertions.test: (() => { const c = new AbortController(); c.abort(); const r = c.signal.reason; return r instanceof DOMException && r.name === 'AbortError'; })()

assertions.description: AbortSignal.timeout() aborts with a "TimeoutError" DOMException as the reason.
assertions.test: (async () => { const s = AbortSignal.timeout(10); await new Promise((r) => s.addEventListener('abort', r, { once: true })); return s.reason instanceof DOMException && s.reason.name === 'TimeoutError'; })()

assertions.description: Aborting while the fetch promise is still pending rejects that promise with the custom abort reason (the long-standing half of the contract).
assertions.test: (async () => { const c = new AbortController(); const p = fetch('/v153/fetch-api-forward-reason-from-abortcontroller-to-fetch-response/slow-body?chunks=4&delay=150', { signal: c.signal, cache: 'no-store' }); c.abort(new DOMException('conformance pre-response marker', 'TimeoutError')); try { await p; return false; } catch (e) { return !!(e && e.message && e.message.includes('conformance pre-response marker')); } })()

assertions.description: Aborting AFTER the response headers arrived rejects the pending body read with the custom abort reason instead of a generic AbortError. Race-free: the route's hold parameter guarantees the server sends nothing after chunk 1 for 8s, so the tee'd text() read is still pending when the abort fires after the first chunk arrives — regardless of transport buffering. This is the core Chrome 153 fix — expected to FAIL on Chromium before 153 and to pass on Firefox and Chrome 153+.
assertions.test: (async () => { const c = new AbortController(); const res = await fetch('/v153/fetch-api-forward-reason-from-abortcontroller-to-fetch-response/slow-body?chunks=3&delay=100&hold=8000', { signal: c.signal, cache: 'no-store' }); const probe = res.clone().body.getReader(); const body = res.text(); await probe.read(); c.abort(new DOMException('conformance post-response marker', 'TimeoutError')); try { await body; return false; } catch (e) { return !!(e && e.message && e.message.includes('conformance post-response marker')); } })()

assertions.description: A pending response.body reader.read() also rejects with the custom abort reason when the abort lands mid-stream. Race-free: the abort fires after the first chunk has been read while the route's 8s hold guarantees the second read cannot have data yet. Expected to FAIL on Chromium before 153.
assertions.test: (async () => { const c = new AbortController(); const res = await fetch('/v153/fetch-api-forward-reason-from-abortcontroller-to-fetch-response/slow-body?chunks=3&delay=100&hold=8000', { signal: c.signal, cache: 'no-store' }); const reader = res.body.getReader(); await reader.read(); const pending = reader.read(); c.abort(new DOMException('conformance stream marker', 'TimeoutError')); try { await pending; return false; } catch (e) { return !!(e && e.message && e.message.includes('conformance stream marker')); } })()
